thread:
mina park: quick note from the arch huddle  continuous-batcher default still undecided. two pragmatic paths: express (speculative tiny batches) vs dense (coalesce heavy).
ashwin rao: i9m leaning dense default. most tenants want predictable cost and KV locality. express helped a few interactive routes but wrecked some long-context models.
lucy ng: can we compress surface to two knobs? latency_target_ms + cost_sensitivity. runtime maps them to admission + soft_min rules. keep Console simple.
mina park: runtime mapping sketch: if latency_target_ms <= 130 -> express_enabled (bounded budget), else dense_mode with soft_min_batch=6 and coalesce_window_ms=20.
ashwin rao: operational concerns: express fragments KV cache. need auto-disable if kv_miss_rate delta > 10% for 5m OR speculative_tokens > budget*1.1. also cooldown to avoid flip-flop.
lucy ng: suggestion: use priority_score for speculative requests instead of forcing tiny batches. priority_score starts high and decays, so they can join a larger coalesced batch if present  preserves locality.
ops-bot: ALERT: canary-9: batcher.kv_miss_rate up 11% in last 6m
mina park: that alert matches our canary. p95 improved but total GPU_seconds rose ~18%. we need sim numbers.
nashwin rao: i'll add microburst replay into the sim harness and measure p50/p95, kv_hit_ratio, gpu_seconds.
lucy ng: i'll mock Console toggle: mode=(auto|express|dense), latency_target_ms and cost_sensitivity slider. auto surfaces reason when it flips (e.g., kv_miss spike).
mina park: action items: i'll draft RFC with mapping table + auto-disable thresholds + canary plan by Wed. reviewers? ashwin + lucy.
ashwin rao: happy to review.
lucy ng: same. closing until RFC posted. :thumbsup:
_note: Concise Slack thread style. Includes a runtime mapping sketch, an ops bot alert, volunteers and timeline.
